public_payload.normalized_proposition: Given OpenAI's projection to spend $750 billion on compute over the next three-and-a-half years, it will need either to grow revenue to hundreds of billions a year very soon or to raise half a trillion dollars or more over the next few years, at a time when even hyperscalers are having trouble raising that much money.
conditions: given OpenAI's projected $750 billion compute spend over the next three-and-a-half years

statement.excerpt: Putting aside all of the estimates from this piece, OpenAI projects to spend $750 billion in compute in the next three-and-a-half years, which either means it will need to grow its revenue to hundreds of billions a year very soon or raise half a trillion dollars or more over the next few years, at a time when even hyperscalers are having trouble raising that much money.

from_speaker: OpenAI projects to spend $750 billion in compute
grow its revenue to hundreds of billions a year very soon
raise half a trillion dollars or more over the next few years
even hyperscalers are having trouble raising that much money
our_interpretation: The antecedent is the existence of the stated spending projection, rather than expenditure already incurred.
I provisionally use three-and-a-half years from publication as the funding horizon, ending February 4, 2030. The phrases 'very soon' and 'next few years' do not supply separate precise deadlines.

I read 'hundreds of billions a year' as at least $200 billion in realized annual revenue and 'raise' as at least $500 billion in cumulative new financing proceeds, excluding valuation and secondary share sales.
Reaching a threshold would not, by itself, establish that it was necessary. The necessity claim requires a reconstruction of spending, revenue receipts, existing cash and financing.

The projection is treated as a reported estimate. The single metric_scope records the compute-spending antecedent; the revenue and financing alternatives require separate, explicitly reconciled measurements.
criteria.support_condition: Verify the stated $750 billion projection over the stated period, then establish that carrying it out required either at least $200 billion in annual revenue or at least $500 billion in new financing within the interpreted horizon. Contemporaneous evidence must separately establish the claimed hyperscaler financing difficulty.
criteria.contradiction_condition: With the antecedent verified, complete financial records show OpenAI carrying out the projected expenditure within the horizon without either funding threshold, after accounting for existing cash, other obligations and alternative funding sources.
